name: California Wildlands Grassroots Fund

funder.name: Rose Foundation for Communities and the Environment

summary: Quarterly grants of up to US$10,000 for small California groups protecting wildlands, covering stewardship, restoration, equipment and organising as well as advocacy. Mixed advocacy and field work.

amount.note: Maximum grant award is $10,000, and typical grants range between $4,000-$8,000.

fiscal_sponsor.note: Individuals or organisations, sponsored by a nonprofit

reporting: A final grant report is due within one year of receiving the money and before further funding.

eligibility.rule: Keep annual actual expenses and income at $200,000 or less
Be a nonprofit, or be an individual or organization fiscally sponsored by a nonprofit
For urban or suburban projects, connect to larger protected areas or critical wildlife corridors
Include strong environmental advocacy in environmental education programs
Avoid lobbying, beach clean-ups, or film/video production or completion; advocacy outreach using films/videos is allowed

documents: Organizational budget for the current year
Organizational income statement from the most recently completed fiscal year
Project budget and actual income and expenses, if different from organizational statements

eligibility.quote: Annual actual expenses and income of $200,000 or less.
Applicants may be a nonprofit, or an individual/organization fiscally sponsored by a nonprofit.
Project impact must be within the state of California.
Projects in urban or suburban settings, must feature connectivity to larger protected areas and/or be located along critical wildlife corridors.
Environmental education programs must include a strong element of environmental advocacy to be considered.

Lobbying activities as defined by IRS 501(c)(3). Beach clean-ups. Film or video production or completion, although we will fund outreach or communications strategies that use films or videos as advocacy and organizing tools.
